scope: Read-only comparison of published BAM 7.4V raw recordings and 96 new-motor 12V recordings; no hardware access or code modification

methods.tracking_mae: Mean absolute goal-position minus position over raw entries with torque_enable true, converted to degrees; ranges across configurations for specified trajectory and gain. Raw samples are not uniformly weighted in time.
methods.position_derived_speed: Position interpolated on 50ms grid from 0.05 to 5.90 seconds; adjacent differences divided by 0.05; 95th percentile of absolute derivative. Telemetry interpolated at interval midpoints for corresponding 95th percentile.
methods.host_delay: Feedback timestamp minus command_timestamp over powered local raw samples; includes command transmission, explicit 1ms pause and midpoint feedback read time; not physical actuator response latency.

findings.finding: Local 12V position traces show substantially worse fast-motion tracking and roughly half the position-derived speed of reference at P32.
findings.caveat: Different loads, voltage, motor variant and potentially firmware settings prevent motor-only causal attribution. Rate limiting is a hypothesis, not proven cause.

findings.finding: Reference logged speed is roughly 9x lower than position-derived speed, whereas local speed agrees.
findings.hypothesis: Historical commented multiplication by 0.111 in Pypot conversion is consistent with discrepancy; exact reference acquisition driver version is not known.

findings.finding: Reference has unloaded and 0.546/1.084kg loads at 0.10/0.15m; local has 0.1429/0.3061kg tip assemblies plus explicit arm mass at 0.10/0.15/0.20m. Reference arm_mass absent; loader defaults zero.
findings.caveat: Uniform rod and point-tip mechanical model approximates actual mass distribution.

findings.finding: Preserved upstream recorder writes P and D=0 but does not write I; local recorder writes and verifies I=D=0. Historical files do not record I.
findings.caveat: Historical I may have been zero, but that is not established by retained evidence.

findings.finding: New-motor recorder saves P,D,I,lock only; does not set or log acceleration, goal time, goal speed, torque limit or other firmware controls.
findings.caveat: Worn-motor original-settings snapshot cannot retrospectively establish new-motor settings.

findings.finding: Local powered sampling is faster than reference, and command-to-feedback timestamp differences are milliseconds; host timing does not explain the large observed position lag.
findings.caveat: Feedback reads are sequential and midpoint timestamps approximate per-field timing.

findings.finding: BAM STS3215 model explicitly includes target-rate limiting and fitted max_velocity; controller mapping/defaults originate from 7.4V. Log vin overrides default supply voltage, but does not validate controller assumptions for 12V.
Reference includes legacy brutal and unloaded runs; local does not. Both record load and temperature as zero placeholders. Fitting uses metadata vin rather than each measured voltage entry.

recommended_checks: Capture complete firmware/configuration snapshots for both motors with exclusive serial access; include acceleration, goal time, goal speed, torque limits, deadbands, operating mode, voltage and firmware identity where available.
Before interpreting wear, compare identical rig/load/zero/direction/profiles/gains and documented firmware settings.
For reference comparison derive velocity from position consistently, or explicitly validate and correct historical telemetry scaling; preserve original reference data.
Fit distinct 12V parameters including target-rate limit; validate on held-out complete recordings and compare residuals by trajectory, gain and load.
Check actual arm and tip mass distributions before interpreting fitted inertia and friction; retain explicit assumptions.
Investigate voltage outliers separately before assuming they represent sustained supply droop.
caveats: This is a cross-dataset comparison, not a controlled voltage or wear experiment.
No firmware settings or hardware were read by this audit.
Historical reference I and driver version are unknown.
Derived-speed ranges are descriptive percentiles, not fitted physical maximum velocities.
